steps.what: Open the outfit list for the mannequin
Note garments that would not sit

tasks.design: The outfit list is opened from {DOCS}. Dressing mannequins for displays stays in the hands. A list does not dress anything.
tasks.previous_blocker: Outfit lists were a verbal brief at the start of the day.
tasks.enabler_now: The garments for that mannequin can be listed.
tasks.still_hard: Dressing is physical, and the garment may not sit.
tasks.human_edge: The displayer sees a pull the list cannot predict.
tasks.altitude: The list is open. Dressing stays in the hands.

evidence.claim: An outfit list is configuration. The source pack says a locked template can be filled from a table and a person checks it, and that the final selection of a design stays manual.

The source pack says a generated image must be marked, and that naming faces in an archive is biometric data needing explicit consent. This work does not generate the display and does not name faces. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a mannequin is to be dressed and ends when it is dressed.
An outfit has a mannequin id and garment ids, produced by the plan. A garment not on the list is not treated as specified.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the displayer's effort.
A missing sketch, price, or plan is not invented. The displayer does that part by hand.
The incremental hour updates the list when the source row changes.
unknowns: Whether outfits are written down per mannequin.
research_questions: Who accepts a substitution when a garment will not sit?

already_counted.description: The hands-on time is already in the main step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when the outfit is only spoken. Dressing stays physical. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train staff on visual merchandising without scores

steps.what: List daily tasks for staff members
Train staff members on visual merchandising
Note who was shown the task, without a score

tasks.design: Daily tasks are listed from {DOCS}. Supervising or training staff on visual merchandising stays in person. The note records who was shown the task. It stores no score and no ranking.
tasks.previous_blocker: Daily tasks were shown once and then remembered differently.
tasks.enabler_now: The day's tasks can be listed.
tasks.still_hard: Showing someone how to dress a rail is in person.
tasks.human_edge: The displayer sees who did not follow the method.
tasks.altitude: The task list is shared. Training stays in person, and nobody is scored.

reach.task: See who was shown the task
reach.learn: Attendance is not a performance judgement

evidence.claim: A task list is configuration. The source pack says a locked template can be filled from a table and a person checks it, and that the final selection of a design stays manual.

The source pack says a generated image must be marked, and that naming faces in an archive is biometric data needing explicit consent. This work does not generate the display and does not name faces. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when daily visual merchandising tasks are set and ends when attendance at the showing is noted.
A task has an id and a short method, produced by the displayer. The note stores a person id and present or absent. It stores no score.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the displayer's effort.
A missing sketch, price, or plan is not invented. The displayer does that part by hand.
The incremental hour updates the list when the source row changes.
unknowns: Whether daily tasks are written down.
research_questions: Does a note of who was trained need works-council consent?

already_counted.description: The hands-on time is already in the main step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when tasks are not written. Training stays in person. No score is stored. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Pack props and record the count

steps.what: List props and products in the inventory
Maintain inventory records of display items
Write the count the displayer gave

tasks.design: Props, products, and display items are listed from {ERP}. Packing and storing stay physical. The displayer maintains the inventory record by giving the count. The record stores that count and does not invent one.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts were a notebook that purchasing could not read.
tasks.enabler_now: A stock row can be listed, and a count can be written back.
tasks.still_hard: Packing and judging the count stay with the displayer.
tasks.human_edge: The displayer knows a broken piece that should not be counted as fit.
tasks.altitude: The list is current. The count is still the displayer's, and only that count is written.

reach.learn: Which item was packed but not counted as fit

evidence.claim: Writing a count a person entered is configuration. The source pack says a locked template can be filled from a table and a person checks it, and that the final selection of a design stays manual.

The source pack says a generated image must be marked, and that naming faces in an archive is biometric data needing explicit consent. This work does not generate the display and does not name faces. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when props are packed or counted and ends when the count is written.
A stock row has an item id. The count is a number the displayer enters. An item with no count is left blank and is not filled by the screen.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the displayer's effort.
A missing sketch, price, or plan is not invented. The displayer does that part by hand.
The incremental hour updates the list when the source row changes.
unknowns: Whether props and display items are already stock rows.
research_questions: Who else relies on this count?

already_counted.description: Packing time is already in the packing step.

incremental.description: Correct a count when a packed item is damaged.

approvals.approved_version: counts the displayer entered for that pack

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when items are not stock rows. Packing stays physical. A blank count stays blank. The range is below that case.

tasks.short: Produce signage from stored price and text

steps.what: Load the price and the description

loop.purpose: Produce sign text that copies only stored price and description fields.
loop.output: A sign whose every field cites that item id.
loop.check: The price and the description match the stored fields exactly.
loop.stop: Stop when the price or the description is missing.
loop.why_not_simpler: A blank sign cannot show which item the words came from.

steps.what: Release the sign to be printed

tasks.design: Price and description are loaded from {ERP}. Signage is produced on the computers only from those fields, into {DOCS}. The displayer checks it. An unchecked sign is not released. No picture is generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Signs were retyped from a price list, and the amount drifted.
tasks.enabler_now: A price and a description can be copied into a sign layout.
tasks.still_hard: The displayer still checks that the sign is the one for that fixture.
tasks.human_edge: The displayer catches a description that is true in the file and wrong on the floor.

ambition.what: A price change can refresh the sign the same day, and the old amount is not released.

tasks.altitude: Typing the price is gone. Checking the sign before it is printed stays.

evidence.claim: Filling a sign from stored fields is a checkable copy. It is not a generated picture. The source pack says a locked template can be filled from a table and a person checks it, and that the final selection of a design stays manual.

The source pack says a generated image must be marked, and that naming faces in an archive is biometric data needing explicit consent. This work does not generate the display and does not name faces. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a sign is needed and ends when the displayer releases it.
An item has an id, a price, and a description, produced by the price file. A missing field stops the sign. The layout does not draw a picture.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the displayer's effort.
A missing sketch, price, or plan is not invented. The displayer does that part by hand.
The incremental hour updates the list when the source row changes.
unknowns: Whether descriptions are short enough to fit the sign.
research_questions: Who may release a sign that the file and the floor disagree on?

already_counted.description: Checking the sign is already in the check step.

incremental.description: Retire a released sign when its price changes.

approvals.approved_version: sign the displayer checked for that item

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when the price or the description is not stored. An unchecked sign is not released. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Dressing mannequins stays in person. Training is in person and is not a score. Inventory counts are entered by the displayer. Sign text comes from the price file and is checked before release.
reach: A count is the number the displayer entered.
A sign is not printed until the price matches the file.
skills_to_grow: Do not score a staff member.
Do not invent a price that is not in the file.
role.ambitious_version: The price file is open before the sign is cut, and the mannequin is still dressed by a person.
